sentences.text: BY THE PP, ASSAM Advocate for the Petitioner : MS. S G BARUAH Advocate for the Respondent : PP, ASSAM  Page No.# 2/4  BEFORE  HONOURABLE MRS. JUSTICE MITALI THAKURIA  ORDER Date : 23.03.2023 Heard Ms. S. G. Baruah, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr. P.
Borthakur, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State respondent.
This is an application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, praying for grant of pre-arrest bail to the accused/petitioner, who has been languishing in jail hazot in connection with North Lakhimpur P.S. Case No. 39/2023, corresponding to G.R. Case No. 86/2023, under Sections 120-B/468/471/420/406 of the Indian Penal Code.
The Case Diary has been received and I have perused the same.

sentences.text: 1 It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner, Ms. S. G. Baruah, that the accused/petitioner is behind the bar for last 50 days and thus, the I.O. has got ample opportunity to interrogate the accused/petitioner keeping him in custody.
All the required documents have already been collected by the I.O. and hence, further custodial interrogation of the accused/petitioner may not be necessary for the purpose of investigation.

In this context, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Mr. P. Borthakur, has submitted that there are sufficient incriminating materials in the Case Diary against the accused/petitioner and the I.O.
has also achieved substantial progress in the investigation.
But, from the materials in the Case Diary, it cannot Page No.# 3/4 be said that the I.O. will be filing the Charge-Sheet within a short period.
Accordingly, it is submitted that considering the length of detention of the accused/petitioner, his bail prayer may be considered.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for both sides and also considering the length of detention already undergone by the accused/petitioner, i.e. 50 days, I am of the view that the I.O.
has got ample opportunity to interrogate the accused/petitioner in the custody and accordingly,
further custodial interrogation of the accused/petitioner seems to be not necessary here in this case.

Accordingly, it is provided that on furnishing a bond of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand) only with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, North Lakhimpur, the accused/petitioner, namely, Azahar Uddin Ahmed @ Md. Ajaharuddin Ahmed, be enlarged on bail, subject to the following conditions:
(i) that the petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation by the Investigating Officer as and when required;
(ii) that the petitioner shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer; and Page No.# 4/4 (iii) that the petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, North Lakhimpur, without prior permission.
In terms of above, this bail application stands disposed of.
The Case Diary be sent back.
JUDGE
